  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Special Meeting
  March 13, 2024
  10:00 a.m.

ROLL CALL: At 10:28 a.m., on Wednesday, March 13, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in
Ruth Reese Hall of the Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California.

CITY COUNCIL:  PRESENT:  MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  ABSENT:  LEE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director
of Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Chief of
Police Kennedy, Deputy Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen

Also present was Facilitator William R. Kelly, President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M24-34

The City Clerk reported that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City Council being
held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of the
Government Code of the State of California.

1. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS – F2M24-4

  1) P.J. GUIDA, 808 N. Bushnell Ave., spoke against Short Term Rentals (STR) and also
  submitted his comments via email which are on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  2) Mary HOSOKAWA, 1037 S. New Ave., discussed the need for more services and
  structured social recreational programs for adults with autism or adaptive recreation
  programs such as those offered by the City of Whittier.

  3) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., spoke regarding trash on the sidewalks, the effects
  of the Bike and Pedestrian Plan on street parking, improvements to the ACT Bus system,
  the effects of new zoning on residential areas for affordable housing, and the problems
  faced by property owners of small and mid-size apartment buildings.

  4) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the incoming Chinatown Service
  Center building, the expansion of the ACT Bus to meet the needs of new customers, the
  incoming Dog Park, the Historic Preservation Ordinance, a proposed project at a
  potential historic site, the need for more affordable housing projects and the preservation
  of existing public art.

  5) Marisol GRIER, via Zoom, requested an addition of an item from the 2023 Strategic Plan,
  the creation of an Old Town Alhambra district.

 2.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M24-33

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William R. Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning session.
  The strategic planning session included, but was not limited to, a discussion of the
  Councilmembers’ SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) Analysis
  Survey results; and, setting tentative goal definitions and priorities.

  Mr. KELLY began by summarizing the 6 goals prioritized by Council in the previous year and
  as outlined in the staff report, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. He further provided
  updates as to which goals were completed or ongoing.

  Mr. KELLY outlined the strengths and weaknesses as identified by Council. Council went on
  to list additional strengths such as environmental sustainability projects, outreach to the
  community, improvements to City website, and. Council added additional weaknesses to the
  list such as blight, vacant buildings, illegal dumping, and. Council discussed the weakness
  listed. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed additional changes to the City
  website to assist Senior citizens. Councilmember MALONEY highlighted the “Mobile City
  Hall” program, and suggested expanding the service to senior facilities such as the Joslyn
  Adult Center.

  Mr. MALONEY and Mr. KELLY discussed the listed weakness of “Partisan politics affecting
  city business.” Mayor MAZA discussed the listed weakness of “High rent compared to other
  local cities,” and suggested ways to promote or assist the increase of housing stock. Mr.
  MAZA further discussed the need to emphasize Economic Development, real versus
  perceived community opposition to projects, and partisan politics affecting city business. Ms.
  PÉREZ elaborated on her comments regarding blight, Mr. Maza’s comments regarding the
  need for economic development with regards to East Main Street and Valley Boulevard, and
  working with the Chamber of Commerce. Mr. MAZA suggested seeking an outside
  consultant to assist with economic development.

  Mr. KELLY went on to discuss the listed opportunities for Council discussion. Ms. PÉREZ
  discussed seeking more “Place Making Centers” as it related to economic development,
  walkability, and urban planning. She also discussed the proposed Community Center and
  expressed hope at the positive effect it may have on the area. Ms. PÉREZ discussed the
  idea of seeking a food hall business as a game changer for the economic corridor. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the potential transportation opportunities to CSULA that
  were being worked on by METRO in connection with the projects leading up to the Los
  Angeles Olympics event. She further suggested seeking youth interns for assistance with the
  strategic planning sessions.

  Mr. MALONEY discussed changes made to the proposed development at 801 E. Main due
  to zoning changes and further spoke regarding the need to attract developers while engaging
  with the community. He also discussed the Bicycle and Pedestrian Plan and opportunities for
  the City to purchase private properties for development.

  Mr. MAZA discussed strengths and opportunities such as an influx of job openings with
  SkyZone, developing more amenities such as the Community Center to increase walkability
  on Valley Blvd., the other community benefits from the proposed Community Center,
  development potential along East Main Street, and improvement with keeping streets clean
  by increased bulky item pickups.

  2
3-13-24
   Ms. PÉREZ recounted her observations of surrounding cities in the San Gabriel Valley and
  the walkability of neighborhoods with wide sidewalks and mature trees. She discussed the
  need to be more mindful of tree trimming and planting to increase the tree canopy on the
  major corridors and not just the individual neighborhoods. She explained that this would
  encourage pedestrians and bicyclists. Ms. PÉREZ went on to refer to the identified
  weakness of the removal of historic buildings and the lack of historical elements in new
  developments. Mr. MAZA went on to discuss the proposed development at 801 E. Main St
  and the ways in which the City could work with developers to produce well designed projects.

  Mr. KELLY went on to discuss threats to the City and the ways in which some of them have
  been addressed by the strategic plan.

  In an interactive demonstration, Council each took turns indicating the weaknesses,
  opportunities, and threats which they felt had not been addressed. This included high rent,
  lack of historical design elements in new developments, better connection to CSULA,
  placemaking centers, review building heights on East Main Street, purchase Foundry
  building, economic development on Valley Blvd., more mixed-use development, state
  mandates, traffic issues, pension liabilities, and the disappearance of small businesses. Mr.
  KELLY clarified the next steps in working with staff to review the discussion and reprioritize
  the Strategic Plan goals. He also clarified the steps for presenting the Strategic Plan to
  Council and the public.

  City Manager BINNQUIST suggested that the session break for lunch and afterwards, staff
  and Council could discuss other items which were brought up over the last few months.
  There was a scheduled 30-minute lunch break from approximately 12:00 p.m. to 12:31 p.m.

  Ms. PÉREZ and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed her suggested topic of “Council meeting norms,
  procedures, and decorum.” Ms. PÉREZ clarified that rather than formulate a formal review of
  Council procedures, she would prefer more open communication between Councilmembers.
  City Attorney MONTES and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed various options employed by other
  city councils. Mr. MALONEY continued to discuss and Mr. MONTES provided clarification.
  Mr. MAZA expressed that he also did not want to take up staff’s time to research or draft a
  policy, but rather that Council could make adjustments during the meeting and that he
  wanted to be cautious of placing limitations on Council as the voice of the community. Ms.
  PÉREZ supported comments made by Mr. Montes and Mr. Maza.

  In another interactive demonstration Council reviewed new items highlighted by staff as well
  as the items previously indicated by them, and reassessed their prioritized goals. This
  included incentives for commercial uses on the ground floor of the downtown, speed humps,
  City speed policy, minimum wage, rent stabilization, Council meeting norms and procedures,
  high visibility cross walks and safety measures around school sites, commercial and
  residential design guidelines, and short-term rentals.

  Mr. MAZA and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the commercial design guidelines. Mr.
  MALONEY, Mr. KELLY, and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the traffic calming policy, speed
  humps, and City speed policy. Ms. PÉREZ and Ms. BINNQUIST continued to discuss the
  Active Transportation Plan and the ways a City Speed Policy would apply to specific streets.
  Mr. MALONEY clarified that he would prefer an overall Traffic Calming Policy which would
  employ methods such as speed humps.

  Mr. KELLY asked if there were any prioritized items Council would like to reevaluate. Ms.
  PÉREZ and Mr. KELLY discussed the macro goals versus the granular details. Ms.

   ANDRADE-STADLER requested the addition of student internship opportunities. Mr. KELLY
  clarified the next steps for staff regarding finalizing the Strategic Plan.

  Mayor MAZA thanked Mr. Kelly, staff, the community members, and Council for all their
  work.

ADJOURNMENT:  At 1:00 p.m., Mayor Maza adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
